name: pdra_sync_ifc_mapping
description: Match a contractor's required IFC parameter names against the model's parameters and produce an updated IFC mapping file. Reads the contractor's list, scans the model, proposes matches (LLM), confirms with the user, then writes a safe-renamed output file (timestamp suffix).
author: user

clarificationQuestions.question: Path to the contractor's required IFC names file (e.g. C:\\Project\\contractor-required.txt)?
Path to the existing IFC mapping file? Leave blank to start fresh.
Where should the updated IFC mapping file be written?

args.content: PLACEHOLDER — orchestrator substitutes the merged mapping content built from prior steps.

name: pdra_validate_ifc_mapping_against_model
description: Given an IFC mapping spec (array of {category, revit_parameter, ifc_property, ...}), check that the model has those parameters populated. Reports per-entry status — ok / partial / empty / missing_param / type_mismatch — before exporting to IFC.
author: user

name: pdra_setup_grids_and_levels_from_dwg
description: End-to-end project setup from linked AutoCAD DWGs. Reads the DWG layer holding grid lines and creates Revit grids at exact positions, and reads the layer holding level lines and creates Revit levels at the matching elevations. Both DWGs must already be linked or imported in Revit. Asks the user to pick the link, layer, and units.
author: user

clarificationQuestions.question: Which CAD link contains the grids? (provide the link element id from pdra_list_links)
Which layer in that link holds the grid lines? (e.g. A-GRID)
Which CAD link contains the levels? (id from pdra_list_links — can be the same DWG)
Which layer in that link holds the level lines? (e.g. A-LEVL)
Coordinate units in the DWG?

args.grids: PLACEHOLDER — orchestrator builds the grids array from the read_cad_lines result and pdra_ask_user-confirmed naming.

args.levels: PLACEHOLDER — orchestrator builds the levels array (elevation_mm + name) from the read_cad_lines result.

name: pdra_document_floor_plans

Asks for naming conventions, view templates, sheet number pattern, and title block.

Padding around the grid extents when setting crop boxes, in mm.

name: pdra_kozijnstaat_per_door_type
description: [LEGACY — DO NOT USE FOR ANNOTATED KOZIJNSTATEN] Builds an assembly + assembly-views-based kozijnstaat sheet per door type. Assembly views silently clip API-placed dimensions and spot elevations, so this path produces sheets that need every annotation placed by hand. For an annotation-friendly kozijnstaat, chain: pdra_list_family_types → for each type, pdra_create_kozijnstaat_sections(wall_id, mark) → pdra_apply_view_template → pdra_create_sheet → pdra_place_viewport_on_sheet × 3 → pdra_create_window_door_schedule. This composite stays for projects that intentionally use Revit's native assembly-grouping for non-annotation deliverables.
author: user

clarificationQuestions.question: Which category to build the kozijnstaat for?
Title block to use for the new sheets (id from pdra_list_title_blocks).
Which assembly views should each sheet show? (comma-separated)
Browser folder name for the new sheets (e.g. '200-kozijnstaat').
Assembly + sheet name pattern. {mark} = type Mark, {family} = family name, {type} = type name.
Type marks (or family:type names) to skip — comma-separated, leave blank for none.

args.type_id: PLACEHOLDER — orchestrator iterates per type from pdra_list_family_types. Tool itself picks the first instance. Skip if pdra_list_assemblies already shows one with the resulting name.
args.name: $name_pattern

args.kinds: PLACEHOLDER — split $view_kinds by comma into an array. Tool itself is idempotent — already-existing kinds are skipped.

name: pdra_create_level_matching
description: Create a new level whose extent matches an existing reference level — chooses the cleanest available path. Prefers scope-box inheritance (project-wide, no overrides) when the reference is assigned to one; otherwise copies the reference's model curve direction. The atomic pdra_set_level_elevation already implements the decision; this workflow handles discovery (list existing levels, pick a reference) and naming.
author: user

clarificationQuestions.question: Name for the new level (e.g. '01a tussenverdieping').
Elevation in mm (e.g. 3500 for 3.5 m above project zero; negatives allowed for basements).
Reference level id whose extent the new level should match (id from pdra_list_levels). Leave blank to auto-pick the closest level by elevation.

args.element_id: PLACEHOLDER — reference_level_id (or auto-pick the closest level if 0). Reads Scope Box and Elevation so the orchestrator can decide which match path to expect.

args.elevation_feet: PLACEHOLDER — convert $elevation_mm to feet (mm / 304.8). The atomic accepts feet only.
args.match_extents_from: PLACEHOLDER — reference level id resolved above. The atomic prefers scope-box inheritance when the reference has one, falling back to model-curve copy.

name: pdra_compliance_snapshot
description: Always-on compliance record (1 call): run the model-truth quality checks AND append a metric snapshot to the version-controlled history, so a firm can capture a checkable compliance state at any milestone. Deterministic — both steps source their own data (quality checks scan the model; the snapshot is captured live). Pass commit:'commit'/'push' on a developer install to version the record with the team. Pair with pdra_export_process_trace to get the action trail alongside the state.
author: user

phase.description: Project stage tag for the snapshot, e.g. concept/DO/TO/oplevering.

label.description: Free-form note for this compliance snapshot.

commit.description: Git action on the repo-tracked record (dev mode only): none/commit/push. Default none.
